documents.title: PourIt!: Weakly-supervised Liquid Perception from a Single Image for Visual Closed-Loop Robotic Pouring

passages.text:
The method of Lin et al. [17] only uses the estimated object pose and size for calculating container-tocontainer distance as the initial pouring point. Such a strategy sometimes fails due to an imperfect initial pouring
point, as the transparent bottleneck results in inaccurate object size estimation. Our method only use object pose information to calculate the liquid-to-container distance as feedback to adjust the pouring point, which is less influenced by
the inaccurate size estimation. However, AFA method performs poorly than [17], because the inaccurately estimated
mask of AFA provides the wrong visual feedback to adjust
the pouring point, making the liquid spill out of the target
container instead.
passages.locator: Author-hosted preprint, section 4.3 Results and Analysis, PDF page 8

candidates.statement: A pouring strategy that selects the initial pouring point by calculating container-to-container distance using estimated object pose and size may sometimes fail due to inaccurate size estimation, especially for containers with transparent bottlenecks.

components.description: Strategy: Use estimated object pose and size to calculate container-to-container distance for determining the initial pouring point in robotic pouring.
Requires reliable estimation of object pose and size, which may not be possible when containers have transparent bottlenecks.
Inaccurate initial pouring point can result from size estimation error, possibly leading to pouring failure.
